To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a multi-item, dynamic, production-distribution planning model for a process industry with a multiple parallel bottleneck stage and diverged finishing stages is proposed and tested, and that the proposed model can be used to solve a wide range of production-distribution planning problems in process industries.

the proposed models can be used to solve multi-item, dynamic production planning problems between a manufacturing location with a serial process and a distribution center with general piecewise linear transportation costs.

(i) a tight mixed-integer formulation of the manufacturing system is proposed; (ii) three equivalent mathematical programming formulations for the manufacturer-distributor production flow planning problem are proposed; (iii) the formulations are strengthened by the addition of valid inequalities; and (iv) the addition of extra 0- 1 variables can significantly reduce the computational effort required to obtain optimal solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic production planning problem of a process manufacturing system that is located at the upstream of a supply chain and is connected to a distribution center.

the dynamic planning of production and distribution in the process industry, where the production system at the manufacturer has a serial process with multiple parallel machines and divergent finishing machines.
the production-distribution planning of a manufacturer and its distributor, in which transportation costs are represented by general piece-wise linear functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model with the extra 0- 1 variables and valid inequalities performs best in terms of computational efficiency.
the model with the extra 0- 1 variables is the most efficient model for solving the problem under consideration.
, for the problem considered in this paper, the best formulation is the piecewise linear formulation with valid inequalities and extra variables added.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a tight mixed-integer formulation for the serial process with a parallel machines bottleneck stage, a multiple parallel machines finishing stage, and general piecewise linear transportation costs.

we are able to develop an efficient model and algorithm to solve the multi-item dynamic production distribution planning problem in a process industry with a bottleneck stage and diverging finishing stages.
a tight model of the production system and the manufacturer-distributor production planning problem is proposed and a number of strategies for solving the model have been tested and compared.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed models can be applied to solve large-scale problems in a reasonable amount of time.
the use of extra 0- 1 variables can be a very effective way of improving the computational efficiency of a mathematical programming model.
the use of valid inequalities is essential for solving large-scale problems, while the addition of extra 0- 1 variables can improve the efficiency of the branching process.
